title: Where Shall the Man Be Found
description: Where Shall the Man Be Found in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 25, part 2, headed “Divine instruction”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Where shall the man be found That fears t'of-fend his God, That loves the go-spel's joy-ful sound, And trem-bles at the rod?

lines: Where shall the man be found
That fears t' offend his God,
That loves the gospel's joyful sound,
The Lord shall make him know
The wonders of his covenant show,
With such as to his covenant stand,
And love to do his will.
Their souls shall dwell at ease
Their seed shall taste the promises,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
